inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back): FY2023 54, FY2024 65, 9M-2025 61; FY2025 and H1-2026 are untagged, so the TTM figure is an estimate of ~85 (0.5% of revenue). Equity-award withholding taxes were last disclosed at $13m (FY2019) and are immaterial at this scale; no combined figure is published.
inputs.buyback_note: us-gaap:PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock 9M-2025 = 1,576 (last tagged period). Cover-page shares fell from 289.5m (2025-08-01) to 280.0m (2026-07-31), ~9.5m shares retired in twelve months, so the flat count is being funded in cash; the authorization was doubled to $16B with ~$9.9B remaining (Q2 2026). Authorized is not spent: only the tagged financing outflow is recorded.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 2026-06-30 (FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025): revenue 15,026 + 9,802 - 7,726 = 17,102; OCF 8,758 + 5,417 - 4,032 = 10,143; drilling/completion/infrastructure capex 3,523 + 1,929 - 1,806 = 3,646; DD&A 5,038 + 2,565 - 2,363 = 5,240. That window blends H2-2025 at ~$60-65 WTI with Q2-2026 at ~$95, i.e. a ~$73 WTI-equivalent year, which is close to the $70 mid-cycle deck the base case normalises to. Acquisition cash (us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquireOilAndGasProperty, 2,815 TTM incl. Double Eagle and Viper mineral purchases) is excluded from reported FCF; the model correspondingly assumes only organic volume growth.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Friday); Yahoo chart API, 52-week range 137.03-216.90
inputs.share_count_basis: 280,024,353 common shares on the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-31). Diluted and basic weighted-average counts are identical in every period tagged (Q2 2026: 281.2m), because unvested RSUs are participating securities; there are no convertibles or options of note. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Balance sheet 2026-06-30: long-term debt 11,066 + current portion 1,548 = 12,614 carrying value, less cash 462 = 12,152 (consolidated, includes Viper's borrowings). Management quotes net debt of ~$12.3B on a principal basis. Q2 2026 reduced net debt by ~$1.6B; the 2027 maturity is the next tower.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD rate. 10-year UST 5.18% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-09-25), ERP 4.5%, beta ~1.2 for a large-cap Permian pure-play -> cost of equity ~10.6%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (BBB investment grade, recent issues 5.2-6.0%), ~4.5% after tax. Capital structure at market ~81% equity / 19% debt (market cap ~$52B vs net debt $12.2B) -> WACC 9.4%, rounded to 9.5%. The same rate is used in all three scenarios: commodity-price risk is charged once, through the scenario price decks and their probability weights, not through a per-scenario discount-rate premium (owner-fcf-adaptations section f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842. Operating lease liabilities are untagged and immaterial (short-term rig and equipment contracts); lease cost is already inside LOE/G&A and therefore inside the EBITDA margin. No lease liabilities are added to net debt and no separate lease line is charged: treatment (B), applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Viper Energy (VNOM) is consolidated, so the modelled flows carry 100% of its royalty cash flow while ~45-55% of Viper belongs to public holders. The minority claim is removed ONCE, in the equity bridge, at the consolidated non-controlling-interest carrying value of 6,085 (Q2 2026 10-Q, 2026-06-30); nothing is leaked from the flows. Book is a floor: VNOM closed at $40.93 on 2026-09-25 and has historically traded at 1.3-1.5x book, so the market value of the minority's claim is plausibly ~$8B, which would take roughly $7/share off every scenario. Viper's post-Sitio share count could not be sourced from a filing (the SEC companyfacts record for the pre-merger Viper entity ends at Q2 2025), so the auditable book figure is used and the sensitivity is disclosed here.
inputs.accounting_note: Diamondback uses full-cost accounting: the $3,652m FY2025 and $1,400m Q1-2026 charges tagged ImpairmentOfOilAndGasProperties are ceiling-test write-downs at trough prices, not cash; they explain the FY2025 operating margin of 8% and the Q1-2026 EPS of $0.08. Net interest expense is small (FY2025 -244, H1-2026 -119) because interest on unproved properties is capitalised. Cash tax: current tax expense was 785 (FY2024) and 846 (FY2025), 17-19% of pre-impairment pre-tax income, and 818 for H1-2026 (~19% of pre-impairment pre-tax) - IDC expensing, bonus depreciation and Viper's partnership structure keep the cash rate below the 21% federal + Texas margin tax statutory blend. The model uses 20%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), mid-cycle variant for a commodity-price cyclical, routed via dcf-methods (operating company, cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. WHY THIS MODEL: Diamondback is an operating E&P whose value is a stream of free cash flow, but that stream is dominated by the oil price, which sat at ~$95 WTI in Q2 2026 against ~$60-65 through most of FY2025. Capitalising the spot-price cash flow would capitalise a cyclical peak, so the three scenarios are three long-run price decks - bear $60, base $70, bull $85 WTI (nominal, 2027) - each carrying its own revenue, margin, DD&A and capital-intensity consequences, and the year-1 growth rate is the step from the ~$73 TTM base to each deck. Volumes are organic only (FY2026 guidance 522+ MBO/d oil, 1,000+ MBOE/d total, capex ~$3.9B; management's preliminary 2027 run-rate of ~$1.0B/quarter holds production roughly flat). Buybacks are value-neutral here (SBC expensed, count flat). Interest income is not stripped: this is a net-debt company. Working capital capture is zero: no deferred-revenue mechanics in an E&P. Terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF, the low end of the method's cyclical range, because E&Ps deplete: Gordon at 9.5%/1.5% is 12.7x, so the cap binds marginally in the base case.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests (Viper Energy public holders and other) at book
equity_bridge.note: Q2 2026 10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30. Flows are 100% consolidated; the minority's claim is deducted here once. See inputs.nci_treatment for the market-value sensitivity (~$7/share).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment, not a historical CAGR: ~1-2% organic oil volume growth plus ~2% nominal price escalation, tapering to a 1.5% terminal rate as inventory depletes
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (34%) diverges from revenue (40%) and EPS (negative, FY2025 base is after a $3.65B ceiling-test write-down). All three series are dominated by the Endeavor merger (Sep-2024, ~$26B, share count 178m -> 291m), the Double Eagle acquisition (Apr-2025) and the 2020-2022 oil price cycle; none describes organic growth and none is used as the projection driver.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - drilling/completion/infrastructure capex - SBC): FY2022 4,416; FY2023 3,284; FY2024 3,481; FY2025 5,153; TTM Jun-2026 6,412. The 3-yr CAGR of 5.3% is on a per-company, not per-share, basis and reflects the merger; per-share FCF has grown faster because the count is now falling. Reported vs owner FCF differ by only ~1% (SBC is 0.5% of revenue), so the SBC-growing-faster-than-cash-flow warning does not apply. Capex before FY2022 is not in the XBRL pull, so no 5-yr FCF CAGR is computed.

base.narrative: $70 WTI mid-cycle deck from 2027, escalating ~2%/yr nominal; oil volumes +2%/yr to 2030 then +1%. Year-1 revenue ~16.9B (oil ~530 MBO/d at ~$68 realised = 13.2B, NGL ~2.1B, gas ~0.9B after Waha differentials, midstream/royalty/purchased-oil ~0.8B). EBITDA margin 68% (FY2025 cash EBITDA was ~66-68% at ~$64 WTI after hedge gains; Q2 2026 ~71% at $95). DD&A 30.5% of revenue (~$14/BOE post write-down, Q2 2026 run-rate 1,272/qtr) drifting to 29% as the merger step-up burns off. Capex 23.5% (~$3.98B, matching the ~$3.9B FY2026 budget and the ~$1.0B/qtr 2027 run-rate) drifting to 25.5% as Tier-1 inventory matures. Cash tax 20% on EBIT. Year-1 owner FCF ~6.2B (36.6% margin), which ties to the TTM levered figure of 6.4B once the ~$0.25B net interest is added back and the ~$73 TTM price is normalised to $70.

bull.narrative: $85 WTI sustained: management's thesis that depleted global and strategic inventories must be refilled proves right, and the 2026 spike settles into a higher plateau rather than mean-reverting. Year-1 revenue ~20.5B (+20% on the TTM base). Margin 71.5% (per-BOE costs are fixed, so price flows through at ~93% after production taxes; hedges cap some of it). Oil volumes +3%/yr, funded within a capex line that rises to ~$4.5B (22% of revenue) with service-cost inflation. DD&A 26% of the larger revenue base. Barnett gas, the EOR surfactant pilot and Bryant Ranch power are treated as inventory-life support inside the 2% terminal growth, not as separate value. Same 9.5% WACC and 12x cap.

bear.narrative: $60 WTI for the decade: OPEC+ keeps spare capacity flowing, demand growth disappoints, and a US crude export restriction widens the WTI-Brent discount (the spread puts blunt but do not remove this). Year-1 revenue ~14.5B (-15.5%). Volumes are held flat - capital goes to holding production and to the 2027/2029-32 maturity towers, not growth - so revenue grows only with ~1.5% inflation. Margin 65% falling to 62% as fixed per-BOE costs and Waha basis blowouts bite. Capex is cut to ~$3.75B but rises as a share of revenue (26% -> 29%) because Tier-1 inventory depletes and the rig count needed to hold volumes climbs. DD&A 35% of revenue falling to 32% after further ceiling-test write-downs. Terminal growth 1%. Same 9.5% WACC and 12x cap; the balance sheet survives (net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x at $60) so this is a value case, not a solvency case.

scenario_narratives.base: The bull/bear axis for Diamondback is the long-run oil price, then capital intensity as the Permian matures. Base: $70 WTI mid-cycle from 2027 with ~2% nominal escalation, organic oil growth of 1-2%/yr inside a ~$4B capital programme, a 68% cash EBITDA margin drifting to 66.5%, capex creeping from 23.5% to 25.5% of revenue as Tier-1 inventory is consumed, and a 12x cap on terminal owner FCF. The $12.2B Endeavor debt is deducted once and the Viper minority is deducted once at book. Year-1 owner FCF ~6.2B ties to the trailing twelve months after normalising the ~$73 blended price to $70.
scenario_narratives.bull: $85 WTI sustained as the inventory-refill thesis plays out; margin 71.5%, oil volumes +3%/yr, capex ~$4.5B, Barnett gas / EOR / Bryant Ranch power absorbed as inventory-life support inside a 2% terminal rate. Year-1 revenue ~20.5B.
scenario_narratives.bear: $60 WTI for a decade with a widened WTI-Brent discount; flat volumes, margin 65% -> 62%, capex rising to 29% of revenue to hold production, DD&A cut by further ceiling-test write-downs, terminal growth 1%. Net debt/EBITDA stays ~1.3x, so the downside is a value case rather than a going-concern case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 growth-company default. The dominant driver is the long-run oil price, whose distribution around a $70 mid-cycle is roughly symmetric over a ten-year horizon, so bear and bull get equal weight. Bear is not lifted above 25% because net debt is ~1.0x EBITDA at mid-cycle and ~1.3x at $60 with an investment-grade balance sheet and no covenant pressure - the bear case destroys value, not the company. Bull is not lifted despite spot sitting at ~$95, because the bull case requires that spike to become a decade-long plateau, which the 2014, 2020 and 2025 troughs argue against.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF: value the company on a normalised $70 oil deck rather than the ~$95 spot that produced the record Q2 2026 print. SBC is trivial (0.5% of revenue) so house and street bases nearly coincide; the valuation swing is almost entirely the price deck and the terminal multiple. Net debt and the Viper minority are each charged exactly once in the bridge; interest is not in the flows (unlevered) and leases are inside EBITDA. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF because reserves deplete.
key_risks_to_valuation: Oil price: each $10/bbl of long-run WTI is ~$1.9B of revenue and ~$1.4B of after-tax owner FCF, roughly $50-60/share at the model's multiple - the price deck is the valuation
Terminal multiple: at 9.5% WACC the 12x cap binds in the base case; at 10x the base value falls by roughly a tenth
Viper minority marked at book (6,085): at VNOM's market value the deduction is ~$2B larger, about $7/share

Capital intensity: the model lets capex/revenue rise 2pp over the decade; if Permian well productivity decays faster (Analysis: inventory depletion is a moderate risk) maintenance capex climbs and every scenario loses value
Cash tax: 20% assumes IDC expensing and bonus depreciation persist; a move to the ~23% statutory blend costs ~$0.2B/yr of FCF
Debt maturity towers (2027, 2029-32) refinance at higher coupons in the bear deck - the model's unlevered flows do not see this, the discount rate does
Waha gas basis and any US crude export restriction hit realised prices below the WTI deck; the spread puts hedge only the 2026-27 window
Full-cost ceiling-test write-downs are non-cash but signal the price the reserves were booked at; further write-downs at $60 reduce DD&A and raise cash tax, a second-order negative
